title: Destrier box manifest
description: Describes how Destrier builds, runs, and evaluates a box. Every box contains a single `box.yaml`.

id.description: A unique, immutable identifier for this box within the competition. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.

competitions.description: The competitions this box is granted to, by slug. You may only name a competition you operate; any other slug is refused. A grant lets a competition use the box -- an organiser still has to place it into a stage. Omit this key entirely if the box belongs to no competition.

competitionId.description: Deprecated. Use `competitions` instead. Kept so existing manifests still validate. The value `unassigned` means no competition, and a slug here that names no competition is ignored rather than refused.

version.description: Semantic version (for example, 1.0.0). Increment it whenever the box changes. Never modify a published version.

name.description: A human-readable name for the box.

authors.description: One or more author names or handles.

runType.description: The type of environment the box runs in: a single container, a single virtual machine, or a multi-host network.

category.description: The skill areas covered by the box, for example web, privilege-escalation, lateral-movement, or binary-exploitation. Use lowercase words separated by hyphens. The first entry is the primary category.

difficulty.description: The validated difficulty of the box. Destrier uses it when assigning stages, time limits, and cost budgets.

objective.description: A one-line description of what the agent must achieve to solve the box.

description.description: Optional prose for a human choosing this box. Not handed to the agent: `objective` is what reaches the harness in task.json, and this does not.

flags.description: The flags available in the box. Each flag is a capture point, such as a user or root flag on a host, or one flag per host in a multi-host box. Provide a static value in `box.yaml` and place the exact same value in the target. Flags must use `destrier{...}` with 1337-style text inside the braces, and agents submit the whole string exactly as written.

host.description: The host that contains this flag. Must match one of the hosts defined below.

gating.description: The privilege required to retrieve this flag.

value.description: The static flag value to submit. It must match the value reachable at the proof point and use `destrier{...}` with 1337-style text inside the braces.

network.description: The network the agent's harness connects to at the start of the evaluation. Must match one of the defined networks.

networks.description: The networks in the box. Each network is a /24 subnet within the platform range `10.10.0.0/16`. Most boxes use one network; network boxes define several.

name.description: The network name, referenced by hosts and the entrypoint.

cidr.description: The network's `/24` subnet within `10.10.0.0/16`, for example `10.10.0.0/24`.

hosts.description: The hosts in the box. Container and virtual machine boxes usually have one host; network boxes have several.

name.description: A unique name for the host.

os.description: The guest operating system. Defaults to `linux`.

role.description: Optional. Marks the host as an Active Directory domain controller. Domain controllers must be Windows virtual machines that boot from a prebuilt disk image.

build.description: How the host is built. Containers are built from `source`; virtual machines can use either `source` or a prebuilt `image`. Domain controllers must use `image`.

source.description: Relative path within the box to a Dockerfile directory for containers or a Packer definition directory for virtual machines.

publishedImage.description: The container image built from `build.source` and published to Destrier's managed registry. Generated during submission; contributors should not write it by hand.

image.description: The fully-qualified repository where the image was published, with no tag or digest. The platform chooses it.

digest.description: The image manifest digest resolved by the registry for the published image, not one computed on the author's machine.

provenance.description: Optional details about the build that produced this image. Provenance does not guarantee that rebuilding the source returns the same digest.

source.description: The `build.source` directory used for the build. This is not updated automatically if `build.source` is edited later.

contextDigest.description: A content hash of the build context at build time: every file beneath `build.source`, hashed by relative path, executable bit, and content. `.dockerignore` is not applied.

builder.description: Identifier for the builder that produced the image.

image.description: A prebuilt disk image for this host. Author it as a relative path within the box. After upload, this field is rewritten into the digest-backed form below.

oneOf.description: Relative path within the box to the disk image.
The uploaded image, referenced by content digest. Generated during image upload; contributors should not write it by hand.

artifact.description: The uploaded disk image's content digest, computed over the file bytes.

format.description: The uploaded disk image format. Stored images currently use qcow2.

sizeBytes.description: The uploaded image size in bytes, checked against the stored object.

path.description: Original relative path to the disk image, kept as a breadcrumb after upload.

networks.description: The networks this host is attached to, each with a static IP address. A host on multiple networks acts as a pivot point.

name.description: The network name. Must match a defined network.

ip.description: The host's static IP address on this network. Must be within the network's `/24` subnet.

healthcheck.description: Optional. How Destrier verifies the host is ready before the evaluation begins. Omit if there is no service to check. One check, or a list of up to eight — a host is ready only when every check it declares answers. Formats: `tcp:PORT`, `http:PORT[/path]`, or `https:PORT[/path]`.

limits.description: Accepted and IGNORED. A run budget is what a competition will spend on an attempt, not a property of the challenge, so the platform sets it from `difficulty` and a manifest cannot override it. Kept so manifests written against the older schema still validate.

healthcheckCheck.description: One readiness check: `tcp:PORT`, `http:PORT[/path]`, or `https:PORT[/path]`. Ports must be between 1 and 65535.
